item.title: On equational $\mathfrak{X}$-domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.31753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups containing all abelian groups. We introduce and investigate equational $\X$-domains as a generalization of equational domains in algebraic geometry over groups. We characterize these groups by means of systems of equations associated with the identities of $\X$, and describe the radical and coordinate group of the union of two coordinate axes. We also extend classical characterizations of coordinate groups of irreducible algebraic sets, involving discrimination and universal theories, to the setting of equational $\X$-domains. Finally, we establish two construction results: under suitable malnormality, amalgamated free products are equational $\X$-domains; moreover, a restricted regular wreath product of two nontrivial groups is an equational $\X$-domain if and only if its base group is an equational $\X$-domain.
item.dc:creator: Omar Al-Raisi, Mohammad Shahryari

item.title: The optimal exponent in the Babai-Goodman-Pyber theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.32149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Babai, Goodman and Pyber proved that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le [X:H]^c$ for every finite group $X$ and every soluble subgroup $H\le X$, where $\operatorname{Rad}(X)$ denotes the largest soluble normal subgroup of $X$. We prove that the least possible value of $c$ is $b_0=1+\log_9(168\cdot 24^{1/3})\approx3.8141$. For nonsoluble $X$, we obtain the stronger inequality $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le 24^{-1/3}[X:H]^{b_0}$, and the coefficient $24^{-1/3}$ is optimal for this exponent. We reduce the problem to bounds on soluble subgroups of automorphism groups of finite simple groups. Examples based on $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ establish sharpness.
item.dc:creator: Shaowu Zheng

item.title: New families of vertex-transitive quaternionic lattices in products of trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.32587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe infinite families of quaternionic arithmetic lattices in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_1)\times \cdots \times \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ acting transitively on the vertices of the Cartesian product $\mathcal{T}_1\times \cdots \times \mathcal{T}_n$, where $\mathcal{T}_1,\dots, \mathcal{T}_n$ are regular trees. We present an algorithm to determine a presentation for each of these lattices. We also introduce a method for constructing such lattices that act regularly on the set of vertices. We illustrate our results with numerous explicit examples, including several families of known cases, as well as many new instances in arbitrary characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Justin Vast

item.title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two. If the choice must be made equivariantly from independent vertex labels, every edge is forced. In this expository note we follow these two answers through other groups. Geometry alone forces a positive gap on each non-elementary hyperbolic Cayley graph, while on one four-regular nilpotent Cayley graph the choice of action realizes every additive cost in $[1,2]$. The minimum of the action spectrum recovers the geometric cost. Open problems are presented in the end.
item.dc:creator: Itai Benjamini

item.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Weaver

item.title: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.33084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.
item.dc:creator: Alba Gonz\'alez, Tejas Mittal, Andrew Wood

item.title: Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2611.31420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Fagan, Jon McCammond

item.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.31657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.
item.dc:creator: Alan Xuelun Hou, Tudor Popescu

item.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.31759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(\Gamma)$ is edge-transitive, then $\Gamma$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(\Gamma)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Zai Ping Lu, Hai Ze Wang

item.title: A Sylow reduction for isomorphisms of Cayley graphs on abelian groups of cube-free order
item.description: arXiv:2611.32366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The isomorphism problem for Cayley graphs is one of the fundamental problems in algebraic combinatorics. Dobson studied this isomorphism problem and asked whether, assuming that the group generated by the left regular representation and its conjugate under an isomorphism admits a complete sequence of normal block systems, the isomorphism problem for Cayley digraphs on a finite abelian group of cube-free order can be reduced to the corresponding problem on its Sylow subgroups. We answer this question affirmatively. We first prove that color-preserving isomorphisms preserving the fiber partition on direct products $A\times H$ of abelian groups of coprime orders, where $|H|$ is a prime or the square of a prime, have a product decomposition property. Applying this property successively to the Sylow subgroups of a cube-free-order abelian group $G$, we show that if two colored binary Cayley structures on $G$ are connected by a color-preserving isomorphism $f$ for which $\langle G_L,f^{-1}G_Lf\rangle$ admits a complete sequence of block systems, then they are also connected by a color-preserving Sylow coordinate isomorphism. This yields the corresponding Sylow reduction for solving sets.
item.dc:creator: Tingzeng Wu, Liang Qin, Yong Yu, Xing Gao

item.title: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33073v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|\Gamma|'$ $\Gamma$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $\nu_{\Gamma,n,U}$, where $\Gamma$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|\Gamma|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $\Gamma$. The $\Gamma$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_\Gamma(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-\kappa r^2-\zeta r}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $\kappa>0$, and $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $\Gamma$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $\Gamma$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $\Gamma$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $\Gamma$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $\Gamma$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $\Gamma$ (with multiplicity one).
item.dc:creator: Mark Shusterman, Gonen Zimmerman

item.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2503.08411v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(\Gamma_1)$ and $A(\Gamma_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $\Gamma_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $\Gamma_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $\theta$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Abbott, Anthony Genevois, Eduardo Martinez-Pedroza

item.title: Computing canonical labellings of finite solvable groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.26030v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a canonical labelling function on the class of finite solvable groups so that two such groups $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic if and only if can$(G)=$can$(H)$. Specifically, can$(G)$ is a group presentation that describes a group isomorphic to $G$, and our description explains how to construct an isomorphism $G\to$can$(G)$. Our approach is motivated by O'Brien's (1993) canonical presentations for finite $p$-groups and utilises ideas from group cohomology first described by Robinson (1982) and automorphism group algorithms developed by Smith (1994), Holt (2001), and others. We also discuss a proof-of-concept implementation for the computer algebra system GAP and comment on the major bottlenecks and open research questions.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Barrera Acevedo, Heiko Dietrich, Max Horn

item.title: The word problem in verbal products of groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.31289v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that nilpotent and metabelian products of groups with decidable word problem have decidable word problem. In contrast, we exhibit families of groups with decidable word problem for which their solvable product has undecidable word problem. In doing so, we exhibit hyperbolic groups with undecidable membership problem in their derived subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Javier Brude, Rom\'an Sasyk

item.title: Non-solvable $2$-arc-transitive covers of the Petersen graph
item.description: arXiv:2503.06979v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While solvable covers of 2-arc-transitive graphs have been studied extensively, non-solvable covers have remained largely unexplored. This paper takes a first step by constructing such covers for the Petersen graph and determining their structural properties.
item.dc:creator: Jiyong Chen, Cai Heng Li, Ci Xuan Wu, Yan Zhou Zhu

item.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
item.description: arXiv:2611.17557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f\to G$ and $Q_f\to G$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free. For a classical knot quandle, the canonical inner augmentation is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot. For every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$, the canonical inner augmentation is also free.
item.dc:creator: Toshiyuki Akita, Sota Takase

item.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
item.description: arXiv:2611.18541v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \Theta_2, \dots$ with $\Theta_k \circ \Theta_j = \Theta_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $\Theta_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. Without freeness the answer reverses: FL(3) contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices, so the lattice analogue of Takahasi's chain condition for free groups fails. The theorem itself is checked by the Agda proof assistant under its safe flags, for free lattices over generators with decidable equality, and its formal proof uses no classical principle: finite searches and an induction on a finite set replace the infinite pigeonhole principle by which a chain yields a coherent chain.
item.dc:creator: William DeMeo, Ralph Freese

item.title: The standard filtration of Leavitt path algebras and topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on
